Header: Aphis spp. in Brassica napus varieties that are suitable as vegetable

Prevention: Field sanitation is vital for prevention of this pest:
Weed the fields whenever weeds get numerous because they can host aphids; Remove alternative hosts of aphids such as
Amaranthus which should be destroyed by uprooting and burying in a dug pit or by controlled burning
Intercropping with strong-smelling plants such as onion, garlic, or parsley keeps some of the aphids away from the rape.
Monitoring: Monitoring should commence soon after crop emergence and must be done until harvest of the crop
Regularly check for curled leaves on plants at least once a week
Turning of the leaves will reveal presence of tiny green, brown or yellow soft- bodied insects on the underside
Alternatively, place yellow sticky traps just after emergence of the crop
If no aphid-transmitted viruses are known from rape in your area, you can tolerate some aphids on your crop.
Then, you may only consider applying direct control measures when there are so many aphids on leaves that they start to curl.
Direct Control: Leaves showing heavy symptoms (curled, small, lots of aphids under side leaves) should be pruned.
Tephrosia leaf extracts 2-4% (200 grams/Kg) can also be spayed.
Spray neem oil products once every week for 4 weeks at a dosage of 4.5 ml/ 10 m2 .
Ask your local agro-input suppliers to organise such products if neem trees do not grow in your area.
Alternatively, spray bifenthrin -based products at 20ml/20L or 1l/ha.
Alternatively, spray pyrethrin -based products at 60g/L or 0.7mls/L (0.7L/ Ha) depending on product.
Restrictions: In most cases, direct chemical control is not justified, because crops can tolerate some aphids, and because green direct control measures usually work sufficiently.
Only in rare cases you may consider applying a chemical.

When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
